title: Final OEIS collection: individual manuscripts and Lean proofs
author: Dev Goyal
ai_disclosure: ChatGPT generated the developments and consolidation in response to Dev Goyal's prompts, with retained upstream and historical credits. Independent human review is pending.

entries.title: Catalan-weighted Stirling periodicity
entries.summary: For every m >= 1 and n >= m, a(n+φ(m)) is congruent to a(n) modulo m. The least positive period of the tail beginning at m exists and divides φ(m); positivity, minimality, and periodicity are all formalized.
entries.qualifications: Known result, credited to Payam Danesh and earlier related Fubini-periodicity work. Source offset zero. Lean proves the explicit finite Stirling sum with the exact integer weight, the totient period, and the least-tail-period properties. The EGF substitution identity is explained and proved in the manuscript but is not separately a Lean theorem. The onset n >= m is sufficient; optimality is not asserted. The stronger Carmichael-period bound is not formalized here.

entries.title: Parity and convergence of an infinite nested reversion
entries.summary: For every n>=0 the coefficient is odd iff n=2^k. Arbitrarily weighted infinite normalized tails exist uniquely over every commutative ring, and a depth-d nest agrees through degree d+1.
qualifications: Convergence means coefficient stabilization of formal series, with no analytic assertion. The source starts at n=1.

entries.title: Square-index residues for theta quotient substitution
entries.summary: The unique constant-one integer solution of A(x/A)=Theta is Theta modulo 4. At n>0 its residue is 2 iff n is a square, and 0 otherwise.
qualifications: The multiplicative unit inverse and compositional inverse are distinct. Analytic convergence and real special values are not proved.

entries.title: Square-index residues for theta product substitution
entries.summary: The unique constant-one integer solution of A(xA)=Theta is Theta modulo 4. At n>0 its residue is 2 iff n is a square, and 0 otherwise.
qualifications: The multiplicative unit inverse and compositional inverse are distinct. Analytic convergence and real special values are not proved.

entries.title: Congruences for exponential coefficients of (exp(x)-1)/cos(2x)
entries.status: two proved conjectures and stronger classification
entries.summary: For n>=1, a(n)=1 modulo 4. For all n>=0, a(n)=2*2^n+3*4^n modulo 5, so 5 divides a(n) iff 4 divides n.
qualifications: These are exponential coefficients n![x^n]A, not ordinary rational coefficients. The literal rational EGF and its uniqueness are formally proved. Modular convolution does not divide by factorials in finite characteristic.

entries.title: Square support in an implicit rational theta equation
entries.summary: The unique implicit integer solution has residue 2 modulo 4 exactly at positive square indices and 0 elsewhere.
qualifications: The formal source is the explicit positive-index formula (2) in OEIS. A separate formal Laurent-series equivalence to the bilateral title is not claimed. No convergence or real special-value assertion is proved.

entries.title: Twice-square support: a corrected rational theta conjecture
entries.status: false conjecture refuted and corrected theorem proved
entries.summary: For n>0 the residue modulo 4 is 2 exactly at twice-square indices, and 0 otherwise. The original square-support claim is false: a(1)=4, a(2)=6.
qualifications: The formal source is the explicit positive-index formula (2) in OEIS. A separate formal Laurent-series equivalence to the bilateral title is not claimed. No convergence or real special-value assertion is proved.

entries.title: Cubic reversion modulo nine and three
entries.summary: The normalized integral source solution is unique. Its square is congruent to x^2+2x^3 modulo 9. For all n,k >= 0, the coefficient of A(x)^(3k)-A(x^3)^k is zero modulo 3.
entries.qualifications: Source offset one. Integral construction, source uniqueness, and genuine compositional inversion are proved. The modulo-three power assertion is a standard Frobenius consequence, not a new general mathematical principle.

entries.title: Two cubic congruences in characteristic three
entries.summary: The normalized integral source solution is unique. As full formal series, A(x)^3 is congruent to A(x^3), and A(x)^2 is congruent to x^2+2A(x^3), modulo 3.
entries.qualifications: Source offset one. Integral construction and source uniqueness are proved. The cube identity is standard Frobenius; the square identity additionally uses the defining equation. Both identities hold at every coefficient index.

entries.title: A sparse residue pattern for a Mahler substitution equation
entries.summary: For n>1 the residue modulo 4 is 2 exactly at n=2^k+1, and 0 elsewhere; A=x+2xC modulo 4, C=x+C^2.
qualifications: The source quotient by x is expressed by the equivalent division-free equation. Analytic claims in the entry are outside scope.

entries.title: Residues of the inverse of an alternating lacunary series
entries.summary: For n>2 the residue modulo 4 is 2 exactly at n=3*2^k, and 0 elsewhere. The integer series is the unique normalized solution of A(A-x)=A^2.
qualifications: The separate empirical sign-run observation is not proved. Integer halving precedes reduction modulo four.

entries.title: A reversion that becomes an involution modulo four
entries.summary: For n>1 the residue modulo 4 is 2 iff n=2^k+1, and 0 otherwise, for the unique normalized integer solution of A(A^2-x^2)=4A^3.
qualifications: Source uniqueness is proved over the integers, not over arbitrary rings with two-torsion. No analytic value or radius statement is claimed.

entries.title: Odd-index evenness in a nested binomial equation
entries.summary: The unique normalized integer solution of D=x+D(x/(1-x))^2 has even coefficient at degree 2n-1 for every n>1.
qualifications: This is the source apparent pattern and a direct characteristic-two square consequence. No analytic interpretation of the nested title is claimed.

entries.title: A modulus-eight lift for a Catalan substitution sequence
entries.summary: For n>2 the residue modulo 8 is 4 iff n=2^k or 2^k+1 with k>=1, and 0 otherwise. Source identities link B=x+B(C)^2 to A(x-x^2)=x+A^2.
qualifications: The exact integral decomposition A=2C-x+4K is proved before reducing modulo eight.

entries.title: Powers of two in a Catalan substitution congruence
entries.summary: For n>1 the residue modulo 4 is 2 iff n is a power of two, and 0 otherwise; the complete series is 2C-x modulo 4.
qualifications: Normalized source equation A(x-x^2)=x+A(x)^2 is constructed uniquely. The standard Catalan parity mechanism is not claimed as a new general result.

entries.title: Congruences for the scaled inverse series A393856
entries.summary: Every positive-index coefficient is one modulo 5. A coefficient is odd exactly when its index is a power of two.
entries.qualifications: The apparent division by the parameter is defined coefficientwise; no division in a residue ring is assumed. Source normalization and uniqueness are part of the checked interface.

entries.title: A complete parity classification
entries.summary: For every n >= 0, a(n) is odd exactly when n modulo 10 is 1, 3, 7, or 9. Every a(2n) is even. For n >= 1, a(2n-1) is even if and only if n=5k-2 for some k >= 1.
entries.qualifications: Source offset zero. The proof concerns the actual third composition and gives every n >= 0. Both source assertions and the stronger complete parity pattern are included.

entries.title: Four congruence proofs for A396099
entries.summary: All four source assertions: positive coefficients odd; residue cycle 1,3,3,1 from degree three modulo four; second-iterate coefficients vanish above degree two; the stated difference has residue two above degree two.
entries.qualifications: All series are constructed from the source equation. General odd-parameter proof credits Sundaram's earlier r=3 result; no global novelty claim. Negative iterates use the genuine compositional inverse.

entries.title: Congruences for an inverse-iterate family
entries.summary: The equation A(A(A(x)))=(1+x)A(A(x)) has a unique normalized integral solution. Every positive-index coefficient is 1 modulo 3. The coefficient at index n of the kth natural iterate is k^(n-1) modulo 3. The full parameter family is included.
entries.qualifications: Source offset one. A396102 is F_3; the original-family existence theorem uses parameter r+1, so r=2 gives its triple equation. All natural iterates and the general positive-parameter family are included. Formal ZMod 0 extensions are not needed for the stated positive-modulus result.

entries.title: A formalized known congruence theorem for A396797
entries.status: Formalization of a known result credited to Shiva Priyan Shanmuga Sundaram
entries.summary: The credited known r=3 case: positive coefficients are one modulo six and all integer iterates have coefficients k^(n-1) modulo six.
entries.qualifications: All series are constructed from the source equation. General odd-parameter proof credits Sundaram's earlier r=3 result; no global novelty claim. Negative iterates use the genuine compositional inverse.

entries.title: Iterate congruences and a phase correction for A396798
entries.status: Seven proved iterate assertions and a refutation/correction
entries.summary: Seven iterate assertions modulo eight, complete natural-iterate coefficient formula, and corrected coefficient block 1,1,5,5 beginning at degree two; false starting-at-one phase refuted.
entries.qualifications: All series are constructed from the source equation. General odd-parameter proof credits Sundaram's earlier r=3 result; no global novelty claim. Negative iterates use the genuine compositional inverse.

entries.title: Every integer iterate of A396807 modulo ten
entries.status: Two proved source assertions, including negative iterates
entries.summary: Every positive-index coefficient is one modulo ten, and the degree-n coefficient of every integer compositional iterate k is k^(n-1) modulo ten.
entries.qualifications: All series are constructed from the source equation. General odd-parameter proof credits Sundaram's earlier r=3 result; no global novelty claim. Negative iterates use the genuine compositional inverse.

entries.title: Parity and binary divisibility for A396843
entries.status: Original proof and generalizations; corrected modulo-nine classification
entries.summary: Oddness for m=3, parity for all integer parameters, exact residues modulo m squared, binary-digit divisibility for the series and its inverse, and the exact minimum prime-exponent criterion.
entries.qualifications: Original repository retained; new consolidation is AI-generated and awaits human review. Danial Asaria is credited for the prior counterexample to the false earlier modulo-nine claim. No new-priority claim.

entries.title: A corrected modulo-sixteen classification for A396844
entries.status: Corrected all-index classification already contained in the original proof package
entries.summary: For n at least two, residue four at n=4^k+1, residue twelve at n=2*4^k+1, and zero otherwise modulo sixteen; includes parity and binary divisibility.
entries.qualifications: The original source claim omitted the first exceptional class. This is a corrected theorem, not a proof of that false clause.

entries.title: Binary parity for a differential power series
entries.status: proved conjecture and additional source assertion
entries.summary: For all n>=0, [x^n]A is odd iff n is a power of two. Also A=x modulo 3, so 3 divides every coefficient above degree one.
qualifications: The source conjecture begins at n=1. Divisibility by three was already stated without a conjecture label. Analytic asymptotics are not proved.
